clinician.final_diagnosis: after pathophysiological analysis and immunohistochemistry, it was found that the primary tumor was a breast tumor and that the gingival tumor was a metastatic tumor from the breast MAC
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old female presented with a non-healing post-extraction gingival wound, swelling, and vegetation. Biopsy of the gingival lesion revealed nests of cells in mucin lakes with occasional tubular arrangements, consistent with adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemistry of the tumor showed it was estrogen-receptor positive, progesterone-receptor positive, GATA-3 positive, and HER2 1+, strongly suggesting a breast primary. Subsequent imaging of the breast identified an expansive soft tissue mass in the left breast with infiltrating lymph nodes. The combination of these findings confirmed the gingival lesion as a metastatic adenocarcinoma originating from a primary breast tumor.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with a non-healing post-extraction gingival wound, swelling, and vegetation.
Histopathological examination of the gingival lesion showed nests of cells in mucin lakes with occasional tubular arrangements, consistent with adenocarcinoma.
Immunohistochemistry of the tumor (gingival lesion) showed it was ER+, PR+, Ki67 30%, HER2 1+, CK7+, CK20+, mammaglobin -, and GATA-3+, indicating a breast origin.
Imaging revealed an expansive soft tissue mass in the left breast (60 × 40 × 35 mm) and infiltrating lymph nodes in the left axilla, identifying the primary tumor site.
The primary tumor was identified as a breast tumor, and the gingival tumor as a metastatic tumor from the breast, based on pathophysiological analysis and immunohistochemistry.
